title: Nothing can install tektonic: the workspace split broke github: refs and no package is on npm
description:
tektonic-46j.5 turned the repo into an npm workspace. The root package.json is now
`tektonic-workspace`, private, with no main/exports/bin. Every consumer installs via
a `github:pfenerty/tektonic` ref, which resolves to that root.

Reproduced today against main:

    npm install github:pfenerty/tektonic
    # -> added 1 package: node_modules/tektonic-workspace
    # -> no dist/, no node_modules, require.resolve('@pfenerty/tektonic') throws

So the install silently succeeds and produces an unbuildable workspace root instead
of the library. Before the split the root WAS @pfenerty/tektonic and carried
`prepare: npm run build`, which is what made the git ref work at all.

The fallback does not exist either: @pfenerty/tektonic is not on the npm registry.
`npm view @pfenerty/tektonic` is a 404, and the newest tag in the repo is v1.4.0 —
the v2.0.0 release (dec7fec) was never tagged or published. So there is no channel,
git or registry, through which a consumer can obtain post-46j.5 tektonic.

Nothing is broken in production only because all three consumers are pinned by
lockfile to pre-split commits:

  ocidex      1c43ce0 (v1.4.0)
  apko-cicd   e698ccd (v1.1.0)
  homelab     ddac5dc (v2.0.0, the last pre-epic main)

Any Renovate bump, any `npm install` against the bare ref, or any fresh clone that
re-resolves will break. apko-cicd is the most exposed: its dependency is the
unpinned `github:pfenerty/tektonic`.

This is what actually blocks the cross-repo acceptance criteria on tektonic-46j.4
("ocidex, apko-cicd and homelab updated in lockstep") and tektonic-46j.6 (the ocidex
uploadSarifStep / _dep-scan.ts validation gate). Neither can be satisfied while the
packages cannot be installed at all.
acceptance_criteria: All three packages are on the npm registry at matching versions, core first; a consumer can install them and the provider packages resolve against the core peer range; trusted publishing is registered so every release after the first goes through a vX.Y.Z tag alone; a smoke test installs the published packages into an empty project and synthesizes a trivial project; the 'Not on the registry yet' note tektonic-46j.16 added to README.md is removed in the same change, since it then describes a state that no longer holds.
notes:
--- audit 2026-09-22, against main at e602c72 ---
Two criteria are further along than the description implies, and one gap is newly documented:
- "The path a consumer should use is stated in the README": the README ALREADY states the
  registry install (`npm install @pfenerty/tektonic cdk8s constructs`, plus the provider
  packages) and documents the three-package layout with the peer-dependency relationship. So
  this criterion needs no wording change — it needs the packages to exist. Until they do, the
  README documents an install that 404s.
- "CONTRIBUTING.md says npm supports no subdirectory for git dependencies, so the git ref is
  no longer a supported install": NOT present. CONTRIBUTING.md still does not say this
  anywhere. Still outstanding.
- CONTRIBUTING.md's one-time-setup section said "the very first publish is manual" in the
  singular, implying one package. Corrected in this session: all three need a manual first
  `npm publish --access public --otp=...`, core first, because @pfenerty/tektonic has never
  been published either (npm view 404, newest tag v1.4.0).

Superseded in part by tektonic-46j.16, which landed both doc changes below.

--- staged for a human, 2026-09-22 ---
This issue is now ONLY the publish itself. Two things were split out so the board shows what
can move without credentials:

- tektonic-46j.16 — the docs half (README says plainly the packages are not on the registry;
  CONTRIBUTING says the git ref is not an install channel). Landed, not blocked on anything.
- tektonic-46j.17 — the apko-cicd + homelab lockstep bump, carried over from tektonic-46j.4.

Everything needed to run the publish is written down and verified; what is missing is
credentials, and a workflow-scoped push for tektonic-46j.11.

Order when you come to do it:
1. Apply the tektonic-46j.11 patch to .github/workflows/publish.yml (exact content in that
   issue's design field). It cannot be pushed from an agent session.
2. Manual first publish of all three, core first, per CONTRIBUTING.md#one-time-setup. All
   three need it, not just the two new packages — @pfenerty/tektonic has never been published
   either. It needs an interactive --otp; a web-login session alone gets a 403.
3. Register the trusted publisher (npm trust github --repo pfenerty/tektonic --file
   publish.yml --allow-publish, or npmjs.com -> Settings -> Trusted Publishers).
4. Bump every packages/*/package.json to the same version, tag vX.Y.Z, push the tag.
5. Remove the "Not on the registry yet" note tektonic-46j.16 added to README.md.

Then tektonic-46j.13 and tektonic-46j.17 unblock, which is the rest of the epic's cross-repo
validation.

title: State the install story honestly while the packages are unpublished
description:
The docs half of tektonic-46j.12, split out because it needs no npm credentials and no
workflow scope — it can land now, while the publish itself waits for a human.

Two things are wrong in the docs today:

1. README's Install section says 'Published to npmjs as public packages — no registry
   configuration or auth needed' and shows 'npm install @pfenerty/tektonic'. That install
   404s: no package has ever been published (npm view is a 404, newest tag is v1.4.0). The
   README documents an install that does not work, with nothing saying so.
2. CONTRIBUTING.md never states that the git ref is no longer a supported install. It was the
   channel every consumer used before tektonic-46j.5, and it now silently resolves to the
   private tektonic-workspace root: 'npm install github:pfenerty/tektonic' adds one package
   with no dist and no bin, and require.resolve('@pfenerty/tektonic') throws. An install that
   fails loudly is fine; one that succeeds and produces nothing is not.
acceptance_criteria: README says plainly that the packages are not on the registry yet and what that means for a consumer today; CONTRIBUTING.md states that the git ref is no longer a supported install, and why (npm has no subdirectory support for git dependencies, and the root is now a private workspace); no claim in either file describes a channel that does not work without saying so.
close_reason: README and CONTRIBUTING now state the install story as it actually is; the note comes out again as part of tektonic-46j.12.

title: The beads JSONL has no working merge protection: a stale branch silently clobbers the issue graph
description:
Reproduced on main, and it has already happened once.

Commit 287b508 branched before c83745b ("bring the 46j epic graph in line with main") and
carried an older .beads/issues.jsonl forward. Merging it overwrote the file wholesale: main
lost the closures of tektonic-46j.1, .2, .3 and .5, and dropped tektonic-46j.11, .12 and .13
entirely. Nothing warned. The damage then propagated — the Dolt database is gitignored, so
the SessionStart hook rebuilds it from that file, and a fresh cloud session was offering work
that shipped weeks ago as `bd ready`, including tektonic-46j.1 whose SynthTarget has been in
the tree since 884da97.

Three defences are supposed to prevent this. None of them is working:

1. `.gitattributes` declares `.beads/issues.jsonl merge=beads`, but the driver is NOT
   configured — `git config --get merge.beads.driver` is unset. A merge driver named in
   .gitattributes but absent from git config is silently ignored; git falls back to its
   ordinary line-based merge on a file where line order carries no meaning.
2. The driver could not work even if configured: the installed bd (0.56.1) has no `bd merge`
   command at all (`bd merge` → unknown command).
3. `.beads/hooks/` holds the shims (pre-commit, post-merge, pre-push, post-checkout,
   prepare-commit-msg) but `bd hooks list` reports every one NOT INSTALLED, and
   `core.hooksPath` is unset with an empty `.git/hooks/`. So the pre-commit export never
   runs (the JSONL goes stale against the database) and the post-merge import never runs
   (the database goes stale against the JSONL).

Worse, CLAUDE.md actively reassured readers this was safe: "bd import is upsert, so merging a
branch's JSONL never clobbers issues it does not mention." True of `bd import`, false of
`git merge`, which is what actually runs. That sentence has been corrected, and the manual
workaround documented, in the same commit that files this issue.

This is P1 because the issue tracker is how work is chosen. A silently wrong graph does not
cause a visible failure — it causes duplicated or abandoned work, which is exactly what
happened.
design:
Make at least one defence real. In rough order of value:

1. Install the hooks in every clone, and make a cold cloud container do it too.
   `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh` already installs bd and rebuilds the database; adding
   `bd hooks install` (or setting core.hooksPath to a committed directory) is a small
   addition to a script that already owns this territory. The pre-commit export is the
   defence that matters most: it keeps the committed JSONL in step with the database, so a
   merge conflicts loudly instead of resolving wrongly.

   Weigh this deliberately rather than just doing it: a pre-commit hook that rewrites
   .beads/issues.jsonl mid-commit changes what every `git commit` in this repo does,
   including agent ones. That is a real behaviour change and the reason this issue proposes
   it rather than shipping it.

2. Either configure a merge driver or stop claiming one. `.gitattributes` naming a driver
   that does not exist is worse than naming none, because it reads as protection. Check
   whether a newer bd ships a merge driver under another name (`bd conflicts` and
   `bd merge-slot` exist and may be the intended path); if none does, replace the line with
   a comment saying the file needs manual reconciliation, so the next reader is not misled.

3. Consider a CI check: a job that imports the committed JSONL into a scratch database and
   fails if the round-trip differs from the file, or if a merge dropped an ID present in
   either parent. `bd doctor` and `bd preflight` may already cover part of this. This is the
   only defence that works regardless of what any individual clone has configured, which
   makes it the most valuable one for a repo whose contributors are mostly agent sessions
   in fresh containers.

Whatever lands, remove the manual workaround from CLAUDE.md's bullet — a documented manual
check is a stopgap, not a fix, and leaving it in place after the real fix invites people to
keep doing it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Merging a branch whose .beads/issues.jsonl is stale either conflicts loudly or preserves both sides; demonstrated with a test merge that reproduces 287b508's shape.
- `.gitattributes` no longer names a merge driver that is not configured and does not exist.
- A fresh cloud container ends SessionStart with the bd hooks actually installed (`bd hooks list` shows them), or with a documented reason why not.
- CLAUDE.md's manual-check workaround is removed once a real defence is in place, and AGENTS.md matches.
notes:
--- another sighting, session cqljcu, 2026-09-22, on main at 9781e41 ---
Not a merge this time, so this is a second failure mode worth recording alongside the first.
A cold cloud container came up with a Dolt database that was BEHIND the committed JSONL:

  bd list showed all 10 epic children of tektonic-46j open, and did not know 46j.12-.15
  existed at all. The committed .beads/issues.jsonl had 21 issues and the correct statuses.

So the SessionStart rebuild either did not run or rebuilt from something older. `bd import
.beads/issues.jsonl` repaired it in one command (7 issues updated, 5 status open -> closed).
The trap: `bd ready` was confidently offering tektonic-46j.1 - the epic's highest-leverage
story, shipped at 884da97 three weeks of commits ago - as the next available work. The only
reason that did not turn into a duplicate implementation is that the source tree already had
synth-target.ts and targets/pac/ in it, which the git log then explained.

Two things that would have caught it cheaply, for whatever this issue ends up building:
- `bd doctor` (or the hook) comparing the DB against the committed JSONL and saying which is
  newer, rather than either one silently winning.
- Noting that `bd import` without --allow-stale skips rows the DB has NEWER copies of. If you
  have already touched an issue this session (I had set 46j.1 in_progress), that one row is
  skipped and stays wrong; --allow-stale restores it.

title: Renovate's ansible manager still parses the generated .tektonic manifests
description:
The Dependency Dashboard (issue #56) lists an 'ansible (8)' section covering .tektonic/tasks/*.k8s.yaml, so the built-in Ansible manager is still matching the generated output by accident of the tasks/*.yaml path — the very bug the custom regex manager was added to solve. It was never actually switched off: ignorePaths does not list .tektonic/**.

Consequence: when gcloud gets a release, the ansible manager proposes an edit to .tektonic/tasks/*.k8s.yaml (generated output) while the regex manager proposes the real fix in gcs-backend.ts. The 'ci images' group rule matches only custom.regex, so the two halves carry different groupNames.

Fix: add .tektonic/** to ignorePaths. Nothing is lost — every versioned pin is covered by the regex manager on the three source files (gcloud in gcs-backend.ts; nodejs/syft/grype in self-ci.ts), and base:stable is unversioned by design.
close_reason: packageRule disables the ansible manager; validated with renovate-config-validator

title: Allow '^npm ci' and '^npm run synth' in self-hosted Renovate allowedCommands
description: renovate.json now carries postUpgradeTasks that re-synthesize .tektonic/ after an image bump. Renovate only runs postUpgradeTasks commands the self-hosted global config permits: allowedCommands must admit '^npm ci' and '^npm run synth' (allowedPostUpgradeCommands on Renovate before v41). Without it the tasks are skipped SILENTLY — the PR looks normal and the manifests fall behind again, caught only by check-manifests turning the Tekton check red. This lives in the Renovate deployment's own config, not in this repo.

title: Add .github/workflows/renovate-synth.yml (needs workflow scope)
description:
The renovate.json custom-manager description references .github/workflows/renovate-synth.yml, but that file could not be pushed from the Claude session that wrote it: the OAuth app credential and the GitHub App token both lack the 'workflow' scope ('refusing to allow an OAuth App to create or update workflow ... without workflow scope' / 'Insufficient scope: required workflow'). Until it lands, grouped image-bump PRs still need a manual 'npm run synth' before they go green; check-manifests catches the drift, so nothing merges silently.

Exact file content to commit at .github/workflows/renovate-synth.yml:

name: renovate-synth

# Renovate's custom regex manager (see renovate.json) bumps the image pins where they
# actually live — in TypeScript — but .tektonic/ is *generated* from those pins, and
# Renovate cannot run the generator. Left alone, every image bump lands as a PR whose
# manifests still name the old tag, and the check-manifests step in the self-CI
# test-npm task fails it on drift, exactly as it is meant to.
#
# postUpgradeTasks is the native fix for this, but it only exists on self-hosted
# Renovate; the hosted app cannot run repository commands. So the synth runs here
# instead: on every push to a renovate/** branch, re-synthesize and commit the result
# back onto the same branch, so the PR carries both sides of the bump.
#
# This does not replace the check-manifests guard — it feeds it. If this workflow ever
# fails to run, the drift still turns the Tekton check red rather than merging quietly.
on:
  push:
    branches: ['renovate/**']

permissions:
  contents: write

# A Renovate rebase can push twice in quick succession; only the newest checkout is
# worth synthesizing.
concurrency:
  group: renovate-synth-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  synth:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          # Matches the Node the Flox environment pins for local work.
          node-version: '24'

      - run: npm ci

      - run: npm run synth

      # Most renovate branches (npm bumps, lock file maintenance) leave the manifests
      # byte-identical, so the common case is a no-op rather than an empty commit.
      #
      # The push uses GITHUB_TOKEN deliberately: pushes made with it do not trigger
      # workflows, so this job cannot re-trigger itself. Tekton PAC watches the branch
      # independently and re-runs the pipeline on the new commit.
      - name: Commit the regenerated manifests
        run: |
          if git diff --quiet -- .tektonic; then
            echo "renovate-synth: .tektonic already matches the pins, nothing to commit"
            exit 0
          fi
          git config user.name 'github-actions[bot]'
          git config user.email '41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'
          git add .tektonic
          git commit -m 'chore: re-synthesize .tektonic for the image bump'
          git push origin "HEAD:${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
close_reason: Obsolete: Renovate is self-hosted, so postUpgradeTasks does the re-synth. No GitHub Actions workflow — all automation belongs in tektonic.

title: Renovate image bumps must carry the re-synthesized .tektonic manifests, and land as one group
description: Renovate's custom regex manager bumps the image pins in examples/self-ci.ts but cannot run 'tektonic synth', so every image-bump PR leaves .tektonic/*.k8s.yaml behind and fails the check-manifests step. Hosted Renovate cannot run postUpgradeTasks, so a GitHub Actions workflow has to re-synth and commit on renovate branches. Also group the apko-cicd image bumps into a single PR instead of one per image.
close_reason: renovate-synth workflow re-synthesizes .tektonic on renovate branches; custom-manager image bumps grouped into one 'ci images' PR

title: Migrate ocidex from tektonic v1.4.0 to 2.x
description:
ocidex is pinned to tektonic v1.4.0 (lockfile commit 1c43ce0) and is the consumer
furthest behind. It is also the one tektonic-46j.6 names as its validation gate, so
this migration is on the epic's critical path rather than incidental cleanup.

Measured today by installing local builds of tektonic into ocidex/.tektonic, the
migration has four parts, in the order they surface:

1. Raw '#!' bodies are a synth error since v2.0.0 (tektonic-k2n.13). The first
   failure is govulncheck-scan/sarif-upload-govulncheck — uploadSarifStep in
   .tektonic/shared.ts. Per tektonic-46j.6's acceptance criteria this should be
   rewritten as an Action rather than merely wrapped in rawScript(), and
   jobs/_dep-scan.ts should lose its buildSteps?: TaskStepSpec[] escape hatch.

2. The provider packages moved out of core in tektonic-46j.5. shared.ts imports
   GitHubStatusReporter from @pfenerty/tektonic, which now throws
   "GitHubStatusReporter is not a constructor". It needs
   @pfenerty/tektonic-reporter-github (and @pfenerty/tektonic-cache-gcs if GCS
   caching is used) as separate dependencies.

3. Injected-step images resolve through project config since tektonic-46j.4.
   ocidex needs to decide between the new neutral fallback and opting back in with
   injectedStepImage: DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE.

4. Extensionless relative imports (`from "./shared"`) work under tsx, which is what
   `make tekton-synth` uses, but not under the 2.x `tektonic` CLI, which runs
   entrypoints on bare node (f61479b). Either keep tsx or add explicit extensions.

Blocked on tektonic-46j.12: none of these packages can be installed yet.
acceptance_criteria:
- ocidex depends on published tektonic 2.x plus the provider packages it uses, with no github: ref.
- uploadSarifStep and jobs/_dep-scan.ts are expressed with the Action API; no TaskStepSpec[] escape hatch and no implicit SARIF path convention remain.
- make tekton-synth and make tekton-check are green, and the .tekton diff is reviewed line by line rather than accepted wholesale — v1.4.0 to 2.x adds param descriptions and HOME=/tekton/home to every pipeline.
- The injected-step image is an explicit choice, not the unpinned fallback, unless that is decided deliberately.

title: Update .github/workflows/publish.yml to publish all three workspace packages
description:
tektonic-46j.5 turned the repo into an npm workspace of three packages, but the publish
workflow still assumes a single package at the repository root. Two things are now wrong:

- The tag check reads ./package.json, which is the private workspace root and carries no
  version field. `require('./package.json').version` is undefined, so the check compares the
  tag against "undefined" and every release fails the guard.
- The publish step runs a bare `npm publish` at the root, which would publish nothing useful
  and never reaches @pfenerty/tektonic-cache-gcs or @pfenerty/tektonic-reporter-github.

The change was written and verified as part of tektonic-46j.5 but could not be pushed: the
session token has neither `workflow` push scope nor the equivalent via the GitHub API, which
refuses any write under .github/workflows/. Applying it needs a human or a token with that
scope. The exact content is in this issue's design field.

Until it lands, cutting a vX.Y.Z tag will fail at the version check rather than publish
something wrong — so this blocks a release but cannot cause a bad one.
design:
Replace the two steps below in .github/workflows/publish.yml. Everything else in the file is
unchanged.

--- the tag check ---

      # The tag must name the version being published, or a mistagged release would
      # quietly publish whatever happens to be in package.json. The three packages version
      # together for now (see CONTRIBUTING.md#releasing), so one tag governs all of them.
      - name: Check the tag matches every package version
        run: |
          tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          for pkg in packages/*/; do
            version=$(node -p "require('./${pkg}package.json').version")
            if [ "$tag" != "$version" ]; then
              echo "tag ${GITHUB_REF_NAME} does not match ${pkg}package.json version ${version}"
              exit 1
            fi
          done

--- the publish step ---

      # Re-running a release workflow is routine, and republishing an existing version is
      # an npm error - treat "already there" as success. The provider packages take
      # @pfenerty/tektonic as a peer dependency, so core goes first: a consumer installing
      # the reporter the instant it appears must find the core version it asks for.
      - name: Publish
        run: |
          for pkg in packages/tektonic packages/tektonic-cache-gcs packages/tektonic-reporter-github; do
            name=$(node -p "require('./${pkg}/package.json').name")
            version=$(node -p "require('./${pkg}/package.json').version")
            if npm view "${name}@${version}" version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "${name}@${version} is already on the registry, nothing to do"
              continue
            fi
            npm publish -w "${name}"
          done

Ordering matters: core publishes first so the peer range the providers declare is already
satisfiable the moment they appear on the registry. The per-package "already there" skip
keeps a re-run of a partly-failed release safe.

One-time setup, per CONTRIBUTING.md#releasing: trusted publishing is configured on a package
that already exists, so the first publish of each NEW package (tektonic-cache-gcs,
tektonic-reporter-github) is a manual `npm publish --access public --otp=...` before the
workflow can take over.
acceptance_criteria: A vX.Y.Z tag whose version matches every packages/*/package.json publishes all three packages; a mismatched tag fails the guard naming the offending package; re-running a release is a no-op for packages already on the registry.
notes:
Blocker re-confirmed a THIRD time on 2026-09-22, from both directions again, on a fresh
session with a different token. This is environmental, not stale:

1. git push of a commit touching .github/workflows/publish.yml:
     ! [remote rejected] ... (refusing to allow an OAuth App to create or update workflow
     `.github/workflows/publish.yml` without `workflow` scope)
2. GitHub API create_or_update_file against the same path:
     Insufficient scope: required "repo workflow"

The change was re-applied and re-verified before being backed out, so re-applying it stays
mechanical — the exact content is in this issue's design field and reproduces the file
verbatim. Verified this session against main at 91b02c8:
- YAML parses; the job still has 8 steps.
- All three packages are at 2.0.0, and both providers declare peer @pfenerty/tektonic ^2.0.0,
  so the core-first publish order in the design is the one that matters.
- Tag loop: GITHUB_REF_NAME=v2.0.0 passes; v2.1.0 exits 1 with
  "tag v2.1.0 does not match packages/tektonic-cache-gcs/package.json version 2.0.0".
- `npm publish -w <name> --dry-run` resolves all three: @pfenerty/tektonic (190 files),
  @pfenerty/tektonic-cache-gcs, @pfenerty/tektonic-reporter-github.

Applying this needs a human, or a token with `workflow` scope. Nothing else about it is
open — it is not waiting on a decision.

Standing correction, unchanged: @pfenerty/tektonic has never been published either
(`npm view` 404, newest tag v1.4.0), so ALL THREE packages need a manual first
`npm publish --access public` before trusted publishing can take over — not just the two
new ones. That manual step is tektonic-46j.12's, and it is also human-scoped.

--- blocker re-confirmed a FOURTH time, 2026-09-22, session cqljcu, on main at 9781e41 ---
Both directions again, on a different token, same result:
1. git push of the commit touching .github/workflows/publish.yml:
   ! [remote rejected] ... (refusing to allow an OAuth App to create or update workflow
   .github/workflows/publish.yml without `workflow` scope)
2. mcp__github__create_or_update_file against the same path, on a branch the SAME token
   had just created successfully: Insufficient scope: required "repo workflow".
So branch creation and ordinary file writes work; the workflow path specifically does not.

Re-verified the design content against the working tree before backing it out:
- npm install is needed FIRST in a cold cloud container. node_modules/@pfenerty/* holds
  the workspace symlinks and they were absent; without them `tsc -b` fails with TS2307
  "Cannot find module @pfenerty/tektonic" in both providers, and the publish dry-run
  ships 2 files per provider (README + package.json, no dist) while looking successful.
  Anyone re-verifying this should check "total files" per package, not just the exit code.
- Tag guard, both legs: GITHUB_REF_NAME=v2.0.0 passes; v2.1.0 exits 1 with
  "tag v2.1.0 does not match packages/tektonic-cache-gcs/package.json version 2.0.0".
- npm publish -w <name> --dry-run resolves all three after npm run build:
  @pfenerty/tektonic 190 files, tektonic-cache-gcs 10, tektonic-reporter-github 10.
- YAML parses; the job still has 8 steps. 608 tests green.
Still human-scoped, and still not waiting on any decision.

title: Model the task/job split: a typed, composable Action primitive
description:
The stated API model is GitLab CI plus the thing GitHub gets right: the distinction
between a JOB (a unit of scheduling — a runner, a pod) and a reusable ACTION (a
versioned, parameterized unit of work with declared inputs and outputs, composed
inside a job).

Tektonic models only the first half:
- `Task` = one Tekton Task = one pod = a job. Has identity, params, results,
  workspaces, caches, a status context.
- `TaskStepSpec` = plain data. No identity, no declared inputs, no declared outputs,
  no version, no reuse mechanism beyond "export a function that returns one".

So composing work INSIDE a pod — the common, cheap case — has no typed abstraction at
all. Evidence from the largest consumer:

- `ocidex/.tektonic/shared.ts` exports `uploadSarifStep`, a hand-rolled step factory
  typed only as `TaskStepSpec`. Its inputs are positional/implicit and its output (a
  SARIF file at a path another step must know) is conveyed by convention.
- `ocidex/.tektonic/jobs/_dep-scan.ts` is a job factory whose options include
  `buildSteps?: TaskStepSpec[]` and `caches?: TaskCacheSpec[]` — untyped escape
  hatches that exist precisely because there is no composable action unit. The syft →
  grype → SARIF sequence inside it is the canonical reusable action, and it is
  expressed as three inline steps plus a comment.

docs/job-libraries.md defines a job library as "a function from an options object to
a `Task`". That is the right answer for jobs, and it leaves the action layer empty.
Without it, the plugin ecosystem this epic is building toward can only ship
whole-pod-sized units — which is the coarse granularity that makes GitLab's
`before_script` copy-paste problem, and Tekton's own one-Task-per-thing catalog
sprawl, what they are.

This is the largest API gap between the code and the vision.
design:
Design an `Action`: a reusable, typed, composable unit that renders to one or more
steps inside a Task.

Sketch to argue with, not to implement verbatim:

```ts
interface ActionDef<In, Out> {
  readonly name: string;
  readonly version?: string;        // for hub publication and pinning
  /** Image the action runs in; overridable by the composing task. */
  readonly image: string;
  /** Declared inputs — typed, not a params bag. */
  inputs: In;
  /** Files/values this action produces, addressable by a downstream action. */
  outputs: Out;
  /** Renders to steps at synth time, given the composing task's context. */
  steps(ctx: ActionCtx): TaskStepSpec[];
}
```

The open questions, which are the actual work of this story:

1. **What is an output, inside a pod?** Tekton `Result`s are task-scoped, string-typed
   and 4KB-capped, so they are the wrong carrier for intra-pod handoff. The honest
   in-pod mechanism is a filesystem path both steps agree on. An action's `outputs`
   should therefore be typed path handles that stringify to that path — the same
   trick `Param`/`Workspace`/`Result` already use — so `syft.outputs.sbom` can be
   interpolated into grype's body with no convention to remember. This is the single
   most valuable part of the design.

2. **Where does an action's output cross a pod boundary?** When a downstream TASK
   needs it, it must become a `Result` (small) or a workspace file (large). Make that
   promotion explicit and typed rather than silent.

3. **Composition into a Task.** Probably `steps: [...]` accepting `TaskStepSpec |
   Action`, so actions and raw steps interleave and nothing existing breaks. Actions
   contribute their params/workspaces/caches upward into the composing task, the way
   a StatusReporter's `requiredParams` already merge in (`task.ts` constructor).

4. **Interaction with the exit-code contract.** An action renders multiple steps; in
   a reporting task, every one of them gets `onError: 'continue'` and exit-code
   capture. An action must not be able to opt out silently — same rule
   docs/job-libraries.md already states for raw `#!` bodies.

5. **Relationship to `HubTaskRef`.** A remote Tekton catalog Task is a JOB-sized
   remote unit, already modelled. An Action is pod-internal. Both are "reusable unit
   from elsewhere" and the naming must not blur them.

6. **Does this subsume `taskPreset`?** See the taskPreset story, which depends on this
   one — presets stamp defaults onto a job, actions compose work inside one, and it is
   worth checking whether one of them stops earning its place.

Validation gate, and the real acceptance test: rewrite ocidex's `uploadSarifStep` and
`_dep-scan.ts` against the draft API. If the rewritten versions are not clearly better
than what is there today — fewer implicit conventions, no `TaskStepSpec[]` escape
hatch — the design is wrong and should be reworked before it ships.

Sequencing: this is independent of the SynthTarget work and can run in parallel.
Do NOT let it block on the hub story; an action might eventually be publishable, but
the hub catalog format is Task-shaped, so publication is a separate concern.
acceptance_criteria:
- An Action type exists with declared, typed inputs and outputs, and renders to one or more steps inside a composing Task.
- Action outputs are typed path handles that stringify to the agreed in-pod path, so a downstream step interpolates them with no naming convention to remember.
- Promotion of an action output across a pod boundary (to a Result or a workspace file) is explicit and typed, never implicit.
- Task steps accept TaskStepSpec | Action; actions merge their params/workspaces/caches upward the way StatusReporter.requiredParams already do.
- An action cannot silently opt out of the exit-code contract; the rule matches the existing one for raw shebang bodies.
- Naming clearly distinguishes an Action (pod-internal) from a HubTaskRef (remote, job-sized).
- Validation gate: ocidex uploadSarifStep and _dep-scan.ts are rewritten against the API and are demonstrably simpler - no TaskStepSpec[] escape hatch, no implicit path conventions. If they are not, the design is reworked before shipping.
- docs/job-libraries.md covers the action layer alongside the job layer.

Code complete on main at db35a22 (PR #59). The API landed:
defineAction / Action / ActionOutput / ACTION_OUTPUT_DIR / ACTION_VOLUME_NAME plus
the ActionDefinition, ActionCtx, ActionOptions, ActionOutputs, ActionStepSpec,
ActionContribution and ActionPromotionOptions types are exported from src/index.ts,
HubTaskRef is exported separately so the pod-internal and remote job-sized units are
named distinctly, and docs/job-libraries.md now covers both layers ("Two layers:
jobs and actions", "The action layer", "Crossing the pod boundary", "What an action
may not do"). Covered by src/lib/core/action.test.ts.

The validation gate is NOT met and is the reason this stays open:

  "ocidex uploadSarifStep and _dep-scan.ts are rewritten against the API and are

That gate is the story's own check on whether the design is right, so closing
without it would discard the point of the story. It is blocked twice over:

1. tektonic-46j.12 — ocidex cannot install post-46j.5 tektonic at all.
2. ocidex is still on tektonic v1.4.0 and does not synthesize against any 2.x build.
   The first thing that stops it is, pointedly, the very code this gate targets:

     Error: tektonic [govulncheck-scan/sarif-upload-govulncheck]: a raw '#!' script
     string is emitted verbatim, so it silently opts out of the exit-code contract
     this task's status reporter reads - a failure here can report green.

   That is uploadSarifStep in ocidex/.tektonic/shared.ts hitting the v2.0.0 breaking
   change from tektonic-k2n.13. So the migration and the validation gate are the same
